From: Priya Shah <priya@thunderhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:15:22Z
Subject: High 429s and timeouts in production after quota tier cutover

Hi Irene,

We pushed the org->project tiering cutover during the maintenance window at 06:30 PT and immediately started seeing elevated 429s and increased request latencies for a subset of our traffic. Error rate jumped from ~0.5% to ~9% over 20 minutes and several timeouts were reported by downstream services. This is affecting our payment processing flow.

Attached is a short span sample and a few log excerpts that show retries and 429s concentrated on project IDs under our EU region. Can you confirm if a rate policy or quota mapping could have been misapplied during the cutover? We need an urgent mitigation — either a rollback to the previous policy or an override for those projects.

We are standing by for a call.

— Priya Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, ThunderHealth
(support@thunderhealth.com)

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:46:11Z
Subject: Re: High 429s and timeouts in production after quota tier cutover

Thanks — quick initial findings:

Summary: during the automated cutover a mapping key for the org-level tiering job was off-by-one for a small set of project IDs. That caused those projects to inherit a lower throughput tier (smaller bucket) than expected. The runtime started returning 429s as token throughput exceeded the unexpectedly lower allotment, and retry behavior amplified the storm.

Evidence: I see the policy diff and the job logs. Sample: project 9472 was mapped to tier "standard-256" instead of "enterprise-2k". Error-rate spike aligns with the job timestamp. I've attached a console-override screenshot (console-override-screenshot.png) and included a short query result: 

-- query result snippet --
project_id | expected_tier | applied_tier
9472       | enterprise-2k  | standard-256
9480       | enterprise-2k  | standard-256
(affected ~11 projects)

Mitigation options:
1) Immediate manual override (console) to reassign the affected projects to enterprise-2k. This is fastest (2–3 min) but manual.
2) Rollback to previous policy version. Safer but requires validation; ~10–15 minutes to propagate.
3) Apply a temporary quota bump at the org level to absorb retries while we push a fix.

I recommend option 1 while we prepare a safe rollback (option 2). If customer agrees, I'll apply the manual overrides and monitor. Will also add short-term retry window smoothing on the proxy layer to reduce retry amplification.

— Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident resolved — summary and next steps

Priya — following up with a short incident summary and next steps.

What happened: the org->project tiering cutover included an incorrect mapping that assigned ~11 project IDs to a lower throughput tier. That caused a localized 429 spike and retries amplified latency and error rates.

What we did: Dev applied manual overrides to reassign affected projects to the expected enterprise-2k tier (manual change 09:08 PT). We also applied a temporary org-level quota bump for 30 minutes while we validated. Post-change metrics: error rate dropped from ~9% to 0.6% within 7 minutes; latency returned to baseline.

Attachments: a draft postmortem (postmortem-draft.md) and the console screenshot of the override. We opened INF-4821 to track the root cause fix and a safe automation patch to prevent off-by-one mapping regressions. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821

Next steps:
- Engineering (Dev): permanent fix for the mapping job + additional unit checks (ETA: 7 days).
- Product ops (Grace): add a preflight validation step to the cutover workflow (ETA: 3 days).
- CS (Marissa): coordinate a customer-facing postmortem and SLA credit discussion (if requested).

Jonas — I have flagged this for an executive update in case ThunderHealth requests credits; will coordinate with finance.

Priya — apologies for the disruption. We'll follow up with a formal postmortem and a timeline for the fix.

— Irene Choi
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
